title: Assisi, 1986
hookLine: leaders of many religions gather in Francis's town to pray for peace, each in their own way

lines: A HILL TOWN FULL OF ROBES.
cards: Saffron, black, white, red: robes of every color fill the streets of a hill town in Italy, the town of Saint Francis. A Buddhist monk walks near an Orthodox bishop.

Rabbis, Muslim leaders, Hindu teachers, Sikhs, Anglican and Lutheran church leaders, and leaders of traditional African and Native American religions have come, because the pope invited them, to pray for peace.
But they won't say one prayer together. Each group goes to its own place to pray its own way. Then they come back to one square and stand side by side.

teach.h: AN INVITATION TO FAST AND PRAY.
teach.b: John Paul the Second called it a World Day of Prayer for Peace, and it worked in four steps. First, the invitation.
He asked the leaders of the world's religions to come to Assisi, the town of Francis, a saint remembered for peace and for meeting a sultan in a time of war.
He asked them to fast and pray, and asked nobody to give up anything they believed.

teach.h: APART: EACH PRAYS IN ITS OWN WAY.
teach.b: Second, apart. Each tradition went to its own church, hall or open space and prayed in its own words and its own way. Catholics didn't lead the others' prayers; nobody was asked to join anyone else's worship.

Third, together. In the afternoon they gathered in front of the basilica of Saint Francis, and one tradition after another offered its prayer for peace aloud while everyone else stood and listened in silence.
As the pope put it, they weren't going to pray together, but they were together in order to pray. Fourth, the worry and the answer.
Some Catholics were uneasy, afraid it would look as if all religions were being blended into one.
The pope answered that this was exactly what wasn't happening: each prayed as itself, with respect, and none pretended the differences away. Later popes have gone back to Assisi in the same spirit.
Jesus says in the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God."
At Assisi, peacemaking began with something modest: standing still while your neighbor prays.

how: Catholic dioceses and the Sant'Egidio community hold interreligious prayers for peace in the spirit of Assisi, where each tradition prays in its own way and the others listen in respectful silence.

games.q: you're planning a day of prayer for peace with leaders of many religions. how do they pray?
o: write one shared prayer for everyone to say.
each prays in its own way, and the others stand by in silence.
only the host church prays; the others watch.
games.why: at Assisi each tradition prayed its own way, then they stood together while each prayed in turn.

practice: Think of the people near you who pray differently, or not at all: a coworker who fasts in another season, a family down the street with a different holy day, a friend who keeps no tradition.
Picture them in that square, praying their own way while you stand quietly beside them. If you pray, pray for peace between religions; if not, simply hold them in mind.
